title: Data Structures — The Shape Is the Trade
subtitle: A 28-minute survey of fourteen structures, each introduced as the fix for what the previous one could not do: contiguity buys addressing and forfeits insertion, linkage buys insertion and forfeits addressing, and every structure after that is another trade made deliberately rather than inherited.

footnotes: 28-minute YouTube survey (`youtu.be/vVL6NFzr0Rg`) covering fourteen structures: array, linked list, stack, queue, deque, hash map, hash set, tree, BST, heap, graph, trie, disjoint set, bloom filter, LRU cache. Contains a sponsor segment around 13:37–14:27, excluded here.

Branches are grouped by the property each structure buys rather than by the video's running order. The video's own spine is a chain — each structure introduced as the fix for what the previous one could not do — and the regrouping preserves that while making the trades comparable.

The through-line worth keeping: no structure is better than another, and every one of them pays for its strength somewhere specific. The array pays for O(1) addressing with rigid size; the linked list pays for cheap insertion with linear search; the bloom filter pays for compactness with a bounded, one-directional lie. Choosing well means knowing which price you are willing to pay.

ZP resonance (my framing, not the video's): several substrate invariants are data-structure properties stated as prose, and the question of whether the structure actually supplies the property has never been asked in one place. Four candidates. (1) The chain is a hash chain, not a Merkle log — tamper-evident with O(n) verification, but no compact inclusion proof, which is exactly what "peer-verifiable by hash equality" and the External Anchor tier's compact-commitment discipline are reaching for. (2) Delegation narrowing is a meet-semilattice claim; stating it as one yields associativity, commutativity, and a decidable validity check instead of per-field imperative logic. (3) `MULTI-DEVICE-OPERATION`'s "causal ordering and merge receipts" is CRDT-shaped and needs vector clocks or dotted version vectors specifically — timestamps would not supply causality. (4) `NodeRegistry`'s strict sequence monotonicity already earns §III.19 detectability structurally, by making a gap observable rather than relying on vigilance — the pattern the other three should follow.

Two structures in this video map onto gaps the mesh survey found the same day: a bloom or cuckoo filter is the textbook fit for `DiscoveryManager`'s replay-nonce tracking, which currently grows an unbounded `HashMap` of `VecDeque`s, and an LRU or time-decayed sketch fits `PeerReputation`'s per-category FIFO cap, whose current eviction drops the oldest event of a category regardless of weight and therefore biases the decay it is meant to model.
